title: Auditable Deletion Orchestration for Multi-Region Residency & Retention
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem statement: Customers in regulated geographies require an auditable, fully automated pipeline to honor deletion/RTBF requests that spans multiple data residency regions and storage backends. Current manual or semi-manual purge flows create timing variability, inconsistent evidence artifacts, and cross-region coordination gaps. We need a single orchestration layer that triggers deletion, verifies downstream erasure, captures immutable evidence (hashes, storage manifests, KMS attestations), and emits a tamper-evident report into the customer audit log and our internal compliance archive.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A deletion request can be submitted via Console, API, or S3-compatible upload and routed to the correct residency zone. 2) Orchestrator issues region-specific purge jobs to all storage backends (object stores, DBs, caches) and waits for verified acknowledgements or runs compensating actions. 3) Each backend returns an evidence artifact (signed manifest, content-hash list, ledger entry) stored immutably in the evidence store. 4) System compiles a single tamper-evident report (PDF + JSON manifest + signature) and delivers it to the customer's compliance endpoint and retains a copy for our 7-year audit retention. 5) End-to-end tests and synthetic RTBF runs produce reproducible logs and pass the verification harness.
design_notes:
- Evidence artifacts should be canonicalized: standardized JSON schema, canonical sorting, content hashes using SHA-256, and signing with a key held in HSM/KMS.
- Use an append-only evidence ledger (S3 with object-lock or a dedicated ledger DB) to avoid accidental mutation.
- Orchestrator must support async workflows: submit -> fan-out -> monitor -> reconcile -> finalize. Provide idempotency keys for retries.
- Provide a lightweight UI in Console showing per-region status, last evidence timestamp, and a link to the compiled report.
- Consider privacy: when partial deletion is required (keep some derived aggregates), evidence should include an explicit 'scope' field listing kept artifacts and rationale.
- Audit logs should include operator actions and timestamps for legal discovery.
technical_decisions: 1) Use Temporal for orchestration to manage long-running cross-region jobs and retries (decision made after spike comparing Step Functions vs Temporal on 2025-12-12). 2) Evidence store pattern: S3 with object-lock + AWS KMS envelope encryption for hosted customers; for Private deployments, pluggable store adapter (on-prem object store or internal ledger). 3) Signing: use a dedicated signing key in HSM (Cloud KMS for hosted). Store signatures alongside manifests; include verification endpoint. 4) Backends: implement a small shim on top of existing deletion APIs for DBs and caches to return a deletion manifest. 5) Verification: provide both synchronous acknowledgement and asynchronous verification windows (e.g., eventual consistency for DB replicas).
tradeoffs:
- Pros: Temporal gives robust retry/backoff and visibility but increases infra complexity and operational cost.
- Pros: S3 object-lock provides immutability guarantees; con is that object-lock lifecycle limits can complicate retention policies.
- Tradeoff: Strict immediate verification may increase customer-visible latency for purge confirmation; we will offer two modes: immediate 'acknowledge request received' vs 'fully verified' with SLA differences.
- Private deployments: additional work required to support different HSM/KMS vendors and offline signing — increases implementation surface.
